entries.meaning: Contend has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Three clubs contend for the title almost every season.
They contended for the championship until the final week.
He has been contending with a knee injury all year.
The defense contends that the evidence was planted.
Critics contended that the law was unconstitutional.
He has long contended that the test is unfair.

senses.head: To compete seriously for something such as a title or a prize
examples: Three clubs contend for the title almost every season.
They contended for the championship until the final week.
He has been contending with a knee injury all year.

senses.head: To claim firmly that something is true, especially in an argument or in court
examples: The defense contends that the evidence was planted.
Critics contended that the law was unconstitutional.
He has long contended that the test is unfair.

entries.contrast: Contend for a prize; contend with a problem or a rival.

entries.meaning: To play much better than an opponent during a game. ---
examples: On a good day they can outplay anyone in the state.
The visitors outplayed us in every position.
We were outplayed from the opening whistle.

entries.meaning: To score more points or goals than the other side. ---
examples: They outscore their opponents by twenty points a game.
Miami outscored Boston 30-12 in the fourth quarter.
Our front line has outscored every other team in the league.
entries.русский: набирать больше очков, обыгрывать по очкам

entries.meaning: To keep going longer than someone else and so win. ---
examples: In this heat the fitter team will simply outlast the other.
She outlasted four opponents to reach the final.
He has outlasted three head coaches at the same club.

entries.meaning: To be so much better than an opponent that the contest is never close. ---
examples: A veteran can outclass a rookie without even running hard.
The champions outclassed us in every department.
Our juniors were badly outclassed by the visiting school.

entries.meaning: To move faster than someone and leave them behind. ---
examples: Very few defenders can outpace him over ten yards.
She outpaced the whole field on the last lap.
He has outpaced every sprinter he has met this season.

entries.meaning: Eliminate has 2 distinct senses.
examples: One more loss will eliminate them from the playoffs.
A late goal eliminated the defending champions.
Two seeded players have already been eliminated.
The new process eliminates most of the paperwork.
We eliminated sugar from her diet.
That bug has been eliminated in the latest update.

senses.head: To knock a team or player out of a competition so that they cannot continue
examples: One more loss will eliminate them from the playoffs.
A late goal eliminated the defending champions.
Two seeded players have already been eliminated.

senses.head: To get rid of something completely
examples: The new process eliminates most of the paperwork.
We eliminated sugar from her diet.
That bug has been eliminated in the latest update.

entries.русский: выбивать, выбить (из турнира); устранять, устранить; ликвидировать, убирать

entries.meaning: To win something definitely, so that no later result can change it. ---
examples: A win tonight would clinch the division.
They clinched a playoff spot with two games to spare.
The title was clinched back in October.

entries.meaning: Dethrone has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Nobody expected a rookie to dethrone the champion.
They dethroned the winners of the last two seasons.
The long-time favorite was finally dethroned in Paris.
The revolution dethroned the king in a single week.
A vote in the assembly could dethrone the young queen.
The last emperor was dethroned in 1912.

senses.head: To beat a champion and take their title away
examples: Nobody expected a rookie to dethrone the champion.
They dethroned the winners of the last two seasons.
The long-time favorite was finally dethroned in Paris.

senses.head: To remove a king or queen from power
examples: The revolution dethroned the king in a single week.
A vote in the assembly could dethrone the young queen.
The last emperor was dethroned in 1912.

entries.русский: свергать, свергнуть (чемпиона); свергать с престола, низложить

entries.meaning: To officially name someone the winner or champion. ---
examples: The league will crown a new champion tonight.
They crowned him rookie of the year.
She was crowned world champion in Oslo.

entries.meaning: To finish high enough in a competition to win a medal. ---
examples: Only three swimmers medal in each event.
He medaled in the two hundred meters.
She has medaled at two straight world championships.
entries.contrast: American English keeps one l: medaled, medaling. British writing doubles it: medalled.

entries.meaning: Equalize has 2 distinct senses.
examples: They need one more goal to equalize.
The striker equalized in the eighty-eighth minute.
United had already equalized twice before halftime.
The valve equalizes the pressure between the two tanks.
The new formula equalized school funding across the state.
Divers wait for their ears to equalize before going deeper.

senses.head: To score a goal that makes the score level again
examples: They need one more goal to equalize.
The striker equalized in the eighty-eighth minute.
United had already equalized twice before halftime.

senses.head: To make amounts or conditions the same as each other
examples: The valve equalizes the pressure between the two tanks.
The new formula equalized school funding across the state.
Divers wait for their ears to equalize before going deeper.

entries.русский: сравнивать счёт, сравнять счёт; выравнивать, выровнять; уравнивать, уравнять
entries.contrast: American spelling uses -ize; British writing often prefers equalise.

entries.meaning: To beat an opponent by a very large margin. ---
examples: On their home field they trounce almost everybody.
We trounced the visitors six to nothing.
They have been trounced in both road games.

entries.meaning: To defeat a team completely and heavily. ---
examples: A healthy squad can rout this team.
The Tigers routed their rivals by forty points.
Our defense was routed in the second half.
entries.contrast: Rout rhymes with out. Do not confuse it with the noun route (a way to go), which Americans say /ruːt/ or /raʊt/.

entries.meaning: Notch has 2 distinct senses.
examples: They can notch their tenth win tonight.
He notched three assists in the opener.
She has notched five victories in a row.
Notch the edge so the rope will not slip.
He notched the stick once for every day.
The post had been notched to hold the beam.

senses.head: To win or record a result and add it to your total
examples: They can notch their tenth win tonight.
He notched three assists in the opener.
She has notched five victories in a row.

senses.head: To cut a small V-shaped mark into something
examples: Notch the edge so the rope will not slip.
He notched the stick once for every day.
The post had been notched to hold the beam.

entries.русский: записывать на свой счёт (победу), одержать; делать зарубку, надрез; зазубрить

entries.meaning: Net has 3 distinct senses.
examples: A striker like that can net twenty goals a season.
She netted the winner in extra time.
He has netted in four straight games.
They net shrimp close to shore.
He netted a trout the size of his arm.
The crew has netted three tons this week.
The store nets about a thousand dollars a day.
The sale netted them forty thousand dollars.
He has netted a tidy profit on the rental.

senses.head: To put the ball into the goal and score
examples: A striker like that can net twenty goals a season.
She netted the winner in extra time.
He has netted in four straight games.

senses.head: To catch a fish or an animal in a net
examples: They net shrimp close to shore.
He netted a trout the size of his arm.
The crew has netted three tons this week.

senses.head: To earn an amount as profit after costs are taken out
examples: The store nets about a thousand dollars a day.
The sale netted them forty thousand dollars.
He has netted a tidy profit on the rental.

entries.русский: забивать, забить (гол); ловить сетью, поймать сетью; получать чистыми, зарабатывать чистого дохода
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (net a goal), intransitive (he netted again on Sunday)
entries.contrast: One short vowel before a final t, so the t doubles: netted, netting.

entries.meaning: Equal has 2 distinct senses.
examples: A time of 9.8 would equal the school record.
She equaled the world record in Rome.
That mark has never been equaled since.
Two plus two equals four.
Three teaspoons equal one tablespoon.
Last year's losses equaled everything we had saved.

senses.head: To match a record or a result that someone else has already set
examples: A time of 9.8 would equal the school record.
She equaled the world record in Rome.
That mark has never been equaled since.

senses.head: To be the same in amount, size, or value as something else
examples: Two plus two equals four.
Three teaspoons equal one tablespoon.
Last year's losses equaled everything we had saved.

entries.русский: сравняться, повторить (рекорд); равняться, быть равным; составлять
entries.contrast: American English keeps one l: equaled, equaling. British writing doubles it: equalled.

entries.meaning: Lap has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The leaders lap the slowest riders twice.
He lapped half the field by mile ten.
Two cars had been lapped before the first pit stop.
The dog lapped water from the bowl.
Kittens lap milk instead of sucking it.
The cat was still lapping at the puddle.

senses.head: To get a whole lap ahead of a slower competitor in a race
examples: The leaders lap the slowest riders twice.
He lapped half the field by mile ten.
Two cars had been lapped before the first pit stop.

senses.head: To drink by scooping up liquid with the tongue, the way an animal does
examples: The dog lapped water from the bowl.
Kittens lap milk instead of sucking it.
The cat was still lapping at the puddle.

entries.русский: обгонять на круг, обойти на круг; лакать, вылакать; пить языком
entries.contrast: One short vowel before a final p, so the p doubles: lapped, lapping.

entries.meaning: To win, especially after a hard struggle. ---
examples: Underdogs rarely triumph on this court.
Spain triumphed on penalties.
She has triumphed over three former champions.
entries.contrast: Triumph over an opponent. The ph is said /f/: TRY-uhmf.

entries.meaning: To win in the end, especially in a close contest. ---
examples: Talent does not always prevail over hard work.
Our team prevailed in a third-set tiebreak.
The home side has prevailed in nine straight meetings.
entries.contrast: Prevail over or against an opponent.

entries.meaning: To lead a team as its captain. ---
examples: She will captain the national team this summer.
He captained the squad for six seasons.
The side has been captained by the same player since 2020.

entries.meaning: Scout has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Clubs scout players as young as fourteen.
They scouted him at a high school tournament.
Our staff has been scouting the opposition all week.
We should scout the trail before we bring the kids.
She scouted four cities before choosing one for the store.
A small team was scouting locations for the shoot.

senses.head: To watch players or opposing teams in order to judge them
examples: Clubs scout players as young as fourteen.
They scouted him at a high school tournament.
Our staff has been scouting the opposition all week.

senses.head: To go and look over a place in advance in order to find something or learn what is there
examples: We should scout the trail before we bring the kids.
She scouted four cities before choosing one for the store.
A small team was scouting locations for the shoot.

entries.русский: просматривать (игроков), вести селекцию; разведывать, разведать; подыскивать, подыскать (место)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (scout a player), intransitive (he scouts for a college team)

entries.meaning: Bench has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The coach may bench him for the final.
They benched their starting goalkeeper.
He was benched after two poor games.
He can bench two hundred and twenty-five pounds.
She benched more than anyone else on the team.
I've been benching three times a week since January.

senses.head: To take a player out of the game and keep them on the bench
body: (сажать на скамейку запасных, оставить в запасе)
examples: The coach may bench him for the final.
They benched their starting goalkeeper.
He was benched after two poor games.

senses.head: To lift a weight while lying on your back on a bench
examples: He can bench two hundred and twenty-five pounds.
She benched more than anyone else on the team.
I've been benching three times a week since January.

entries.русский: сажать на скамейку запасных, оставить в запасе; жать лёжа, выжимать лёжа (штангу)

entries.meaning: Rest has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Runners rest two minutes between intervals.
The manager rested his best players before the cup game.
She has been resting a sore shoulder for a week.
Rest your arm on the pillow.
He rested his elbows on the table.
The ladder was resting against the fence.

senses.head: To stop training or playing for a while so the body recovers
examples: Runners rest two minutes between intervals.
The manager rested his best players before the cup game.
She has been resting a sore shoulder for a week.

senses.head: To place something on a support, or to lean against something for support
examples: Rest your arm on the pillow.
He rested his elbows on the table.
The ladder was resting against the fence.

entries.русский: отдыхать, отдохнуть; давать отдых; класть, положить (на что-л.); опираться, прислоняться
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (rest a player), intransitive (rest between sets)
entries.phrasal verbs: rest on · rest up · rest with

entries.meaning: Huddle has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The players huddle before every snap.
The whole team huddled around the coach.
They were still huddling when the whistle blew.
We huddled around the fire until the rain stopped.
Penguins huddle to stay warm.
Passengers were huddling under the shelter waiting for the bus.

senses.head: To gather in a tight circle to plan the next play
examples: The players huddle before every snap.
The whole team huddled around the coach.
They were still huddling when the whistle blew.

senses.head: To crowd close together, usually because of cold or fear
body: (жаться друг к другу, сбиваться в кучу; прижаться)
examples: We huddled around the fire until the rain stopped.
Penguins huddle to stay warm.
Passengers were huddling under the shelter waiting for the bus.

entries.русский: собираться в кружок (для обсуждения); жаться друг к другу, сбиваться в кучу; прижаться

entries.meaning: To play a practice game that does not count in the standings. ---
examples: The two squads scrimmage every Thursday.
We scrimmaged against the junior team.
They have been scrimmaging in full pads all week.
entries.contrast: Double m in the middle: scrimmage, not scrimage.

entries.meaning: Retire has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Most gymnasts retire before they turn twenty-five.
He retired after the 2022 season.
She has retired from international play but still coaches.
The airline is retiring its oldest planes this year.
The team retired his number the season after he left.
That software has been retired and is no longer supported.

senses.head: To stop competing for good at the end of a career
examples: Most gymnasts retire before they turn twenty-five.
He retired after the 2022 season.
She has retired from international play but still coaches.

senses.head: To take something out of use for good
body: (выводить из эксплуатации, списывать; изымать из обращения)
examples: The airline is retiring its oldest planes this year.
The team retired his number the season after he left.
That software has been retired and is no longer supported.

entries.русский: уходить из спорта, завершить карьеру; выводить из эксплуатации, списывать; изымать из обращения
entries.contrast: Retire from a sport. The ending keeps its schwa: /rɪˈtaɪər/, ri-TY-ur, not ri-TYR.

entries.meaning: To keep a player out of the game, usually because of injury. ---
examples: A hamstring strain can sideline a sprinter for weeks.
The injury sidelined him for two months.
Their captain has been sidelined since March.
entries.русский: выводить из строя (о травме), лишать игровой практики
entries.contrast: Most often used in the passive: he was sidelined by a knee injury.

entries.meaning: Condition has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Coaches condition the squad for six weeks before the season.
He conditioned himself with long runs in the hills.
The team has been conditioning since June.
Ads condition kids to want the newest thing.
Pavlov conditioned dogs to salivate at the sound of a bell.
We have been conditioned to check our phones every few minutes.
I shampoo and condition twice a week.
She washed and conditioned her hair before the party.
Conditioning your hair helps with tangles.

senses.head: To train the body so that it is fit and strong for a sport
examples: Coaches condition the squad for six weeks before the season.
He conditioned himself with long runs in the hills.
The team has been conditioning since June.

senses.head: To train a person or an animal to react in a certain way automatically
examples: Ads condition kids to want the newest thing.
Pavlov conditioned dogs to salivate at the sound of a bell.
We have been conditioned to check our phones every few minutes.

senses.head: To put conditioner on your hair
examples: I shampoo and condition twice a week.
She washed and conditioned her hair before the party.
Conditioning your hair helps with tangles.

entries.русский: готовить физически, тренировать выносливость; приучать, приучить; вырабатывать рефлекс, формировать привычку; наносить кондиционер (на волосы), питать волосы

entries.meaning: Hustle has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Good players hustle on every single play.
She hustled back on defense after the turnover.
He has been hustling for loose balls all night.
Two aides hustled him through the crowd to the car.
Don't hustle me — I'll be ready in a minute.
Security was hustling fans toward the exits.
She hustles — two jobs and a weekend gig.
He hustled for every client on that list.
They have been hustling all year to keep the shop open.

senses.head: To play with constant energy and effort, chasing every ball
examples: Good players hustle on every single play.
She hustled back on defense after the turnover.
He has been hustling for loose balls all night.

senses.head: To make someone move somewhere quickly by pushing or hurrying them
examples: Two aides hustled him through the crowd to the car.
Don't hustle me — I'll be ready in a minute.
Security was hustling fans toward the exits.

senses.head: To work fast and aggressively to make money
examples: She hustles — two jobs and a weekend gig.
He hustled for every client on that list.
They have been hustling all year to keep the shop open.

entries.русский: выкладываться, носиться по площадке; быстро вести, вытолкать, выпроводить; подталкивать; вкалывать, крутиться (ради заработка)
entries.contrast: The t is silent: HUS-uhl, like whistle and castle.

entries.meaning: Relegate has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Two more defeats would relegate the club.
They relegated three teams that year instead of two.
The club was relegated last spring for the first time.
Don't relegate the idea to a footnote.
A knee injury relegated him to the bench.
The story was relegated to page twelve.

senses.head: To move a team down into a lower division at the end of a season
body: (переводить в низший дивизион, понижать в классе)
examples: Two more defeats would relegate the club.
They relegated three teams that year instead of two.
The club was relegated last spring for the first time.

senses.head: To move someone or something to a lower, less important position
body: (отодвигать на второй план, задвигать; переводить на менее важное место)
examples: Don't relegate the idea to a footnote.
A knee injury relegated him to the bench.
The story was relegated to page twelve.

entries.русский: переводить в низший дивизион, понижать в классе; отодвигать на второй план, задвигать; переводить на менее важное место
entries.contrast: Usually passive from the team's point of view: they were relegated, not they relegated.

entries.meaning: To control a game and make sure the rules are followed. ---
examples: Retired players often referee youth games.
He refereed two World Cup finals.
She has been refereeing for fifteen years.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (referee a game), intransitive (he referees on weekends)
entries.contrast: The double e stays in every form: refereed, refereeing — three e's in a row.

entries.meaning: To act as the official who judges play in baseball, tennis, or cricket. ---
examples: Volunteers umpire the Little League games.
He umpired behind the plate for all nine innings.
She has umpired at three US Opens.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (umpire a match), intransitive (he umpires in the summer league)

entries.meaning: Officiate has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Two judges officiate each bout.
He officiated the championship game.
She has been officiating college basketball since 2015.
Who is going to officiate at the wedding?
A retired judge officiated their marriage.
Her uncle has officiated at three family weddings.

senses.head: To serve as a referee, umpire, or judge at a sporting event
examples: Two judges officiate each bout.
He officiated the championship game.
She has been officiating college basketball since 2015.

senses.head: To lead an official ceremony, especially a wedding
examples: Who is going to officiate at the wedding?
A retired judge officiated their marriage.
Her uncle has officiated at three family weddings.

entries.русский: судить (соревнование), выполнять обязанности судьи; проводить церемонию, регистрировать брак, венчать
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (officiate a bout), intransitive (he officiates at college level)

entries.meaning: Foul has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Defenders foul him every time he drives to the basket.
She fouled the shooter with a second left.
He had already been fouled twice in the opening minute.
Runoff from the plant fouled the river.
Smoke from the fires fouls the air for weeks.
The beach had been fouled by oil from the tanker.

senses.head: To break the rules by hitting, holding, or tripping an opponent
examples: Defenders foul him every time he drives to the basket.
She fouled the shooter with a second left.
He had already been fouled twice in the opening minute.

senses.head: To make air, water, or a surface dirty
examples: Runoff from the plant fouled the river.
Smoke from the fires fouls the air for weeks.
The beach had been fouled by oil from the tanker.

entries.русский: фолить, нарушать правила (против игрока); загрязнять, загрязнить; пачкать, испачкать
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (foul the shooter), intransitive (he fouled twice in a minute)

entries.meaning: Caution has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Referees caution players for wasting time.
The referee cautioned both captains.
He had been cautioned earlier in the half.
Police cautioned drivers to stay off the roads.
I would caution against signing anything today.
Doctors have long cautioned that the drug is addictive.

senses.head: To give a player an official warning for breaking the rules
examples: Referees caution players for wasting time.
The referee cautioned both captains.
He had been cautioned earlier in the half.

senses.head: To warn someone that something may be dangerous or unwise
examples: Police cautioned drivers to stay off the roads.
I would caution against signing anything today.
Doctors have long cautioned that the drug is addictive.

entries.русский: выносить предупреждение, показать жёлтую карточку; предостерегать, предостеречь; предупреждать

entries.meaning: To cancel another official's decision by using greater authority. ---
examples: Video review can overrule the referee on the field.
The chair umpire overruled the line call.
His decision was overruled after a replay.
entries.contrast: Two r's meet in the middle: over + rule = overrule.

entries.meaning: Appeal has 3 distinct senses.
examples: The team will appeal the suspension.
She appealed to the tournament committee the same evening.
The red card has already been appealed.
The idea of a long drive doesn't appeal to me.
The show appealed mostly to younger viewers.
The simpler design is clearly appealing to first-time buyers.
Aid groups appeal for donations every winter.
Police appealed for witnesses to come forward.
The family is appealing for information about their son.

senses.head: To formally ask for a decision or a punishment to be changed
examples: The team will appeal the suspension.
She appealed to the tournament committee the same evening.
The red card has already been appealed.

senses.head: To be attractive or interesting to someone
examples: The idea of a long drive doesn't appeal to me.
The show appealed mostly to younger viewers.
The simpler design is clearly appealing to first-time buyers.

senses.head: To make an urgent public request for help or information
examples: Aid groups appeal for donations every winter.
Police appealed for witnesses to come forward.
The family is appealing for information about their son.

entries.русский: подавать апелляцию, обжаловать; нравиться, привлекать; быть по душе; обращаться с призывом, взывать; просить (о помощи)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (appeal the ruling), intransitive (appeal to the federation)
entries.contrast: Appeal to a person or body, appeal against a decision. American writing also allows the direct object: appeal the ban.

entries.meaning: Time has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The coaches time every sprint.
They timed her at 11.4 seconds.
All the laps are being timed electronically.
They timed the announcement to land right before the holidays.
If you time it well, you can catch the early train.
The whole campaign was badly timed.

senses.head: To measure how long someone takes to do something
examples: The coaches time every sprint.
They timed her at 11.4 seconds.
All the laps are being timed electronically.

senses.head: To choose the right moment for something to happen
examples: They timed the announcement to land right before the holidays.
If you time it well, you can catch the early train.
The whole campaign was badly timed.

entries.русский: засекать время, хронометрировать; приурочивать, приурочить; выбирать момент
entries.contrast: The silent e drops before -ing: timing, never timeing.

entries.meaning: Clock has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Scouts want to see him clock under 4.5 seconds.
She clocked a personal best in the heats.
The pitcher was clocked at ninety-nine miles an hour.
Say that again and he'll clock you.
The guy clocked him in the jaw.
I got clocked by a stray elbow under the basket.

senses.head: To record a particular time or speed for someone
examples: Scouts want to see him clock under 4.5 seconds.
She clocked a personal best in the heats.
The pitcher was clocked at ninety-nine miles an hour.

senses.head: To hit someone hard, in informal speech
examples: Say that again and he'll clock you.
The guy clocked him in the jaw.
I got clocked by a stray elbow under the basket.

entries.русский: показывать время (о результате), зафиксировать; врезать, съездить (по лицу), ударить

entries.meaning: Dribble has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Young players learn to dribble with both hands.
He dribbled past three defenders.
She was dribbling up the sideline when the whistle blew.
Water dribbled down the wall all night.
Juice dribbles out of the carton if you tip it.
He wiped the paint that was dribbling off the brush.

senses.head: To move the ball along with small touches or bounces while running
examples: Young players learn to dribble with both hands.
He dribbled past three defenders.
She was dribbling up the sideline when the whistle blew.

senses.head: For a liquid to fall or run in a thin, uneven stream
examples: Water dribbled down the wall all night.
Juice dribbles out of the carton if you tip it.
He wiped the paint that was dribbling off the brush.

entries.русский: вести мяч, обводить; капать, стекать тонкой струйкой
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (dribble the ball), intransitive (dribble up the court)

entries.meaning: To catch or stop a pass that was meant for someone else. ---
examples: Good defenders intercept lazy passes.
She intercepted the ball at midfield and ran.
Two of his throws were intercepted in the first quarter.

entries.meaning: To hit a ball before it bounces. ---
examples: She likes to volley at the net.
He volleyed the cross into the top corner.
The ball was volleyed home from six yards out.
entries.русский: бить с лёта, играть с лёта
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (volley the cross), intransitive (she volleys well at the net)
entries.contrast: Vowel + y, so the y stays: volleys, volleyed — not vollies or vollied.

entries.meaning: Spike has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Their tall hitters spike from the back row.
She spiked the ball straight down the line.
He was spiking well all match.
Gas prices spike every summer.
Cases spiked after the holiday weekend.
Demand has spiked since the storm.
Never leave your drink where someone could spike it.
Somebody spiked the punch at the party.
She is sure her soda was spiked.

senses.head: To hit the ball hard and downward over the net
examples: Their tall hitters spike from the back row.
She spiked the ball straight down the line.
He was spiking well all match.

senses.head: To rise sharply and suddenly
examples: Gas prices spike every summer.
Cases spiked after the holiday weekend.
Demand has spiked since the storm.

senses.head: To add alcohol or a drug to a drink, usually without telling anyone
examples: Never leave your drink where someone could spike it.
Somebody spiked the punch at the party.
She is sure her soda was spiked.

entries.русский: бить сверху (в волейболе), гасить; резко расти, подскочить (о ценах, числах); подмешивать, подмешать (алкоголь, наркотик) в напиток

entries.meaning: To hit or throw the ball in a high slow curve over someone. ---
examples: Try to lob the ball over the goalkeeper.
She lobbed the return over his head.
He has been lobbing every short ball all afternoon.
entries.contrast: One short vowel before a final b, so the b doubles: lobbed, lobbing.

entries.meaning: To hit a golf ball gently along the green toward the hole. ---
examples: He can putt better than anyone on tour.
She putted from thirty feet and made it.
He was putting for birdie on the last hole.
entries.русский: бить патт, катить мяч в лунку (гольф)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (putt the ball), intransitive (he putts beautifully)
entries.contrast: Putt rhymes with cut /pʌt/; the everyday verb put is /pʊt/. Both, confusingly, give putting.

entries.meaning: Punt has 2 distinct senses.
examples: On fourth down they usually punt.
He punted from his own end zone.
The ball was punted fifty-two yards.
Let's punt on that until we have real numbers.
The committee punted, sending the whole bill back to staff.
Congress has punted on the issue three years running.

senses.head: To kick the ball after dropping it from your hands, giving it to the other team
examples: On fourth down they usually punt.
He punted from his own end zone.
The ball was punted fifty-two yards.

senses.head: To decide not to deal with something now and to leave it for later or for someone else
examples: Let's punt on that until we have real numbers.
The committee punted, sending the whole bill back to staff.
Congress has punted on the issue three years running.

entries.русский: выбивать мяч с рук, делать пант; откладывать (решение), отложить; пасовать, уходить от ответа
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (punt the ball away), intransitive (on fourth down they punt)

entries.meaning: Bat has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Left-handers usually bat against right-handed pitching.
He batted .310 last season.
She has been batting leadoff all year.
Don't bat your lashes at me — I know you broke it.
She batted her eyelashes at him and he turned red.
He signed the check without batting an eye.

senses.head: To take your turn hitting the ball with a bat
examples: Left-handers usually bat against right-handed pitching.
He batted .310 last season.
She has been batting leadoff all year.

senses.head: To open and close your eyelashes quickly, often to charm someone
examples: Don't bat your lashes at me — I know you broke it.
She batted her eyelashes at him and he turned red.
He signed the check without batting an eye.

entries.русский: отбивать (в бейсболе), бить битой; хлопать (ресницами), моргнуть
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (bat the ball into left field), intransitive (she bats third)
entries.contrast: One short vowel before a final t, so the t doubles: batted, batting.

entries.meaning: In baseball, to tap the ball softly instead of swinging at it. ---
examples: With a runner on first, you bunt.
He bunted the runner over to second.
She was bunting for a base hit, not a sacrifice.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (bunt the runner over), intransitive (he bunted to move the runner)

entries.meaning: To roll a heavy ball down a lane to knock over pins. ---
examples: We bowl every Tuesday night.
He bowled a perfect game in March.
They have been bowling in the same league for years.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (bowl a 250 game), intransitive (we bowl on Tuesdays)

entries.meaning: Field has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Shortstops field more balls than anyone else.
He fielded the ground ball cleanly and threw to first.
The ball was fielded on one hop.
The coach fielded questions for twenty minutes.
She fields about fifty calls a day.
He was fielding complaints all morning.
The party will field a candidate in every district.
They fielded their strongest team in years.
The school has never fielded a girls' hockey team before.

senses.head: To catch or stop a ball that has been hit into play
examples: Shortstops field more balls than anyone else.
He fielded the ground ball cleanly and threw to first.
The ball was fielded on one hop.

senses.head: To deal with questions or calls one after another as they come in
examples: The coach fielded questions for twenty minutes.
She fields about fifty calls a day.
He was fielding complaints all morning.

senses.head: To put a team, a candidate, or a group of people forward to take part in something
examples: The party will field a candidate in every district.
They fielded their strongest team in years.
The school has never fielded a girls' hockey team before.

entries.русский: принимать мяч (в защите), играть в защите; отвечать на (вопросы), принимать (звонки), разбирать (обращения); выставлять, выставить (команду, кандидата)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (field a grounder), intransitive (he fields well)

entries.meaning: Sack has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Their front four sack the quarterback on almost every third down.
He sacked the quarterback three times.
Our passer was sacked six times in one half.
Invading armies usually sack the capital first.
The soldiers sacked the village and burned the fields.
Rome was sacked in 410.

senses.head: In football, to tackle the quarterback before he can throw
examples: Their front four sack the quarterback on almost every third down.
He sacked the quarterback three times.
Our passer was sacked six times in one half.

senses.head: To rob and destroy a captured town or building
examples: Invading armies usually sack the capital first.
The soldiers sacked the village and burned the fields.
Rome was sacked in 410.

entries.русский: сбивать квотербека с мячом, делать сэк; разграблять, разграбить; учинять разгром

entries.meaning: In football, to rush extra defenders at the quarterback. ---
examples: They blitz on almost every passing down.
The defense blitzed and forced a fumble.
He has been blitzing off the edge all night.
entries.русский: идти в блиц, бросать защитников в атаку
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (blitz the quarterback), intransitive (they blitz on every down)
entries.contrast: Ends in -tz, so the third person adds -es: blitzes.

entries.meaning: Pivot has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Keep one foot down and pivot.
He pivoted and shot over the defender.
She was pivoting toward the basket when she was fouled.
The company decided to pivot toward subscriptions.
They pivoted from hardware to software after two bad years.
The campaign is pivoting to a message about jobs.

senses.head: To turn on one foot while keeping the other foot planted
examples: Keep one foot down and pivot.
He pivoted and shot over the defender.
She was pivoting toward the basket when she was fouled.

senses.head: To change to a different strategy or direction, especially in business or politics
examples: The company decided to pivot toward subscriptions.
They pivoted from hardware to software after two bad years.
The campaign is pivoting to a message about jobs.

entries.русский: разворачиваться на опорной ноге, делать пивот; менять курс, сменить направление; переориентироваться
entries.contrast: The stress is on the first syllable, so the t does not double: pivoted, pivoting.

entries.meaning: Curl has 2 distinct senses.
examples: He can curl a free kick around the wall.
She curled the ball into the far corner.
The shot was curled just inside the post.
Her hair curls in humid weather.
She curled her hair for the wedding.
The leaves were curling at the edges.

senses.head: To bend the flight of a ball with spin, especially on a kick or shot
examples: He can curl a free kick around the wall.
She curled the ball into the far corner.
The shot was curled just inside the post.

senses.head: To form into a curved or spiral shape, especially of hair
examples: Her hair curls in humid weather.
She curled her hair for the wedding.
The leaves were curling at the edges.

entries.русский: закручивать, закрутить (мяч); виться, завиваться; завивать, закрутить

entries.meaning: Aim has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Aim for the far corner, not the middle.
She aimed at the top of the backboard.
He was aiming low and the goalkeeper saved it easily.
We aim to finish the roof before it rains.
The program aimed to get teenagers reading again.
The new law is aiming to cut traffic deaths in half.

senses.head: To point something at a target before hitting or throwing it
examples: Aim for the far corner, not the middle.
She aimed at the top of the backboard.
He was aiming low and the goalkeeper saved it easily.

senses.head: To plan or intend to do something
examples: We aim to finish the roof before it rains.
The program aimed to get teenagers reading again.
The new law is aiming to cut traffic deaths in half.

entries.русский: целиться, прицелиться; намереваться; стремиться, ставить целью
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (aim the ball), intransitive (aim for the corner)
entries.contrast: Aim at a target you want to hit; aim for a result you want to reach.

entries.meaning: To throw something hard and a long way. ---
examples: Throwers hurl the javelin more than eighty meters.
He hurled the discus past the record line.
The ball was hurled in from deep right field.

entries.meaning: Fault has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Nerves make players fault on easy serves.
He faulted twice and lost the point.
She has faulted on three straight first serves.
You can't fault her for trying.
Nobody faulted his decision to leave early.
The report has been faulted for leaving out the costs.

senses.head: In tennis, to serve the ball into the net or outside the service box
examples: Nerves make players fault on easy serves.
He faulted twice and lost the point.
She has faulted on three straight first serves.

senses.head: To find something wrong with someone or with what they have done
examples: You can't fault her for trying.
Nobody faulted his decision to leave early.
The report has been faulted for leaving out the costs.

entries.русский: ошибаться на подаче, сделать фол (в теннисе); винить, обвинять; упрекать, ставить в вину

entries.meaning: To do something so badly that it goes completely wrong. ---
examples: One slip can botch a whole routine.
The goalkeeper botched an easy catch.
The handoff was botched on the goal line.

entries.meaning: Spar has 2 distinct senses.
examples: He likes to spar three rounds a day.
She sparred with two different partners this week.
They have been sparring together since Monday.
The two candidates spar over health care in every debate.
She sparred with reporters for twenty minutes.
They have been sparring about the budget all week.

senses.head: To box or fight in practice, without trying to hurt the other person
examples: He likes to spar three rounds a day.
She sparred with two different partners this week.
They have been sparring together since Monday.

senses.head: To argue with someone in a lively way that is not really hostile
examples: The two candidates spar over health care in every debate.
She sparred with reporters for twenty minutes.
They have been sparring about the budget all week.

entries.русский: проводить спарринг, боксировать в тренировке; пикироваться, препираться; спорить, поспорить
entries.contrast: The r doubles: sparred, sparring. You spar with a partner.

entries.meaning: To take hold of an opponent and struggle with them at close quarters. ---
examples: Wrestlers grapple for position on the mat.
The two fighters grappled against the cage.
They were still grappling when the bell rang.
entries.contrast: Grapple with an opponent — or, figuratively, with a problem.

entries.meaning: To hit someone or something again and again with the fists. ---
examples: He can pummel an opponent for twelve full rounds.
She pummeled the heavy bag for an hour.
He was badly pummeled in the later rounds.
entries.contrast: American English keeps one l: pummeled, pummeling. British writing doubles it: pummelled.

entries.meaning: Jab has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Jab first, then move to your left.
He jabbed his way through the opening round.
She has been jabbing at the body all fight.
He jabbed a finger at the map.
Don't jab the fork into the meat like that.
The nurse was jabbing at his arm, looking for a vein.

senses.head: To hit with a short quick straight punch
examples: Jab first, then move to your left.
He jabbed his way through the opening round.
She has been jabbing at the body all fight.

senses.head: To push something pointed into or toward something
examples: He jabbed a finger at the map.
Don't jab the fork into the meat like that.
The nurse was jabbing at his arm, looking for a vein.

entries.русский: бить джебом, тыкать; тыкать, ткнуть; вонзать, вонзить
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (jab him in the ribs), intransitive (jab and move)
entries.contrast: One short vowel before a final b, so the b doubles: jabbed, jabbing.

entries.meaning: To push aside a blow or a shot instead of taking it full on. ---
examples: Fencers parry and then attack in the same motion.
The goalkeeper parried the shot over the bar.
He has parried everything they have thrown at him.
entries.contrast: Consonant + -y becomes -ies and -ied: parries, parried, but parrying keeps the y.

entries.meaning: Knock has 3 distinct senses.
examples: One clean right hand can knock a fighter down.
He knocked his opponent into the ropes.
She was knocked off the ball far too easily.
Somebody is knocking at the door.
She knocked twice and waited.
Knock before you come in.
Don't knock it until you've tried it.
Critics knocked the plan as too expensive.
He's always knocking somebody else's work.

senses.head: To hit someone or something hard enough to move it or bring it down
examples: One clean right hand can knock a fighter down.
He knocked his opponent into the ropes.
She was knocked off the ball far too easily.

senses.head: To hit a door with your hand so that the people inside hear you
examples: Somebody is knocking at the door.
She knocked twice and waited.
Knock before you come in.

senses.head: To criticize someone or something, often unfairly (informal)
examples: Don't knock it until you've tried it.
Critics knocked the plan as too expensive.
He's always knocking somebody else's work.

entries.русский: сбивать, сбить (с ног), ударять; стучать, постучать (в дверь); критиковать, раскритиковать; ругать, охаивать
entries.contrast: The k is silent: NAHK, like knee and knife.
entries.phrasal verbs: knock around · knock around · knock back · knock down · knock off · knock off · knock off · knock out · knock out · knock out · knock out · knock up

entries.meaning: To throw your body forward suddenly, usually to reach something. ---
examples: Fencers lunge off the back foot.

entries.contrast: The silent e drops before -ing: lunging, never lungeing.

entries.meaning: Duck has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Duck under the jab and step inside.

She was ducking and weaving for three rounds.
The mayor ducked the question about taxes.
You can't duck this decision forever.
He has been ducking reporters all week.

senses.head: To lower your head or body quickly to avoid being hit
examples: Duck under the jab and step inside.
He ducked the first punch of the round.
She was ducking and weaving for three rounds.

senses.head: To avoid a question or a responsibility
examples: The mayor ducked the question about taxes.
You can't duck this decision forever.
He has been ducking reporters all week.

entries.русский: уклоняться, пригибаться, увернуться; уклоняться, уйти (от вопроса, ответственности)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (duck a punch), intransitive (duck under the rope)

entries.meaning: To bend your knees and lower your body close to the ground. ---
examples: Sprinters crouch behind the blocks before the gun.
The catcher crouched low and gave the sign.
He was crouching in the ready position the whole point.

entries.meaning: To push or hit someone with your elbow. ---
examples: Big men elbow each other for every rebound.
He elbowed a defender and was called for a foul.
She was elbowed in the ribs going for the ball.

entries.meaning: To push against other people while trying to get a better position. ---
examples: Riders jostle for position on the first lap.
The two forwards jostled in the goalmouth.
He was jostling for space near the post.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (jostle a defender), intransitive (jostle for position)
entries.contrast: The t is silent: JAH-suhl, like whistle and hustle.

entries.meaning: To jump over a barrier while running. ---
examples: Very few athletes can hurdle at that speed.

He has been hurdling since his freshman year.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (hurdle the last barrier), intransitive (she hurdles for the college team)

entries.meaning: To jump over or across something, often using a pole or your hands. ---
examples: She will vault last in the rotation.

entries.transitivity: both — transitive (vault the bar), intransitive (she vaults last)

entries.meaning: Dive has 3 distinct senses.

Stock prices dive every time the rumor resurfaces.

We dived to forty feet to see the wreck.
He spent the week diving with a local guide.

senses.head: To jump headfirst into water, or to throw yourself through the air for a ball
examples: Swimmers dive from the blocks at the gun.
The goalkeeper dived to his right and pushed it wide.
She has dived from the ten-meter board twice today.

senses.head: To drop steeply and fast
examples: Stock prices dive every time the rumor resurfaces.
The plane dived toward the runway and pulled up at the last second.
Temperatures have been diving since the front moved through.

senses.head: To swim underwater using breathing equipment
examples: They dive off the Keys every summer.
We dived to forty feet to see the wreck.
He spent the week diving with a local guide.

entries.русский: нырять, нырнуть; бросаться (за мячом); резко падать, снижаться; пикировать; заниматься дайвингом, погружаться с аквалангом
entries.contrast: Americans say both dived and dove for the past. Dived is the regular form and is always safe; the participle is only dived: has dived.

entries.meaning: To move over ice or a hard surface on skates. ---
examples: They skate every morning before school.
He skated two clean programs in a row.
She has been skating since she was four.

entries.meaning: To ride on a skateboard. ---
examples: Kids skateboard in that park all summer.
He skateboarded to school every day last year.
She has been skateboarding for six years.

entries.meaning: To travel or exercise on a bicycle. ---
examples: We bike out to the lake on weekends.
They biked twenty miles before lunch.
He has been biking to work since March.
entries.русский: ездить на велосипеде, кататься на велосипеде
entries.contrast: Informal American for ride a bicycle. The silent e drops: biked, biking.

entries.meaning: To ride a bicycle, especially for sport or exercise. ---
examples: They cycle along the river every Sunday.
She cycled across the state in five days.
He has been cycling competitively for a decade.

entries.meaning: To come down a snowy slope standing on a snowboard. ---
examples: They snowboard every weekend in winter.
He snowboarded down the back bowl in the fresh powder.
She has been snowboarding since middle school.

entries.meaning: To slide down a snowy hill on a sled. ---
examples: The kids sled on the hill behind the school.
We sledded until it got dark.
They have been sledding all afternoon.
entries.contrast: One short vowel before a final d, so the d doubles: sledded, sledding.

entries.meaning: To travel on water in a kayak. ---
examples: They kayak on the bay every summer.
We kayaked through the narrow channel.
She has been kayaking since college.
entries.contrast: The final k does not double: kayaked, kayaking, because the stress is on the first syllable.

entries.meaning: To travel on water in a canoe. ---
examples: We canoe down that river every July.
They canoed for three days without seeing anyone.
He has been canoeing since he was a boy.
entries.contrast: The e stays before -ing: canoeing, not canoing. But it drops before -ed: canoed.

entries.meaning: To travel down a river on a raft. ---
examples: Tourists raft the canyon in June.
We rafted the whole gorge in a single day.
They have been rafting that river for twenty years.
entries.русский: сплавляться на рафте, сплавляться по реке
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (raft the canyon), intransitive (we rafted all day)

entries.meaning: To swim just under the surface breathing through a tube. ---
examples: You can snorkel right off the beach here.

They have been snorkeling all morning.
entries.contrast: American English keeps one l: snorkeled, snorkeling. British writing doubles it: snorkelled.

entries.meaning: To stay outdoors in a tent for one or more nights. ---
examples: We camp by the lake every August.
They camped two nights on the ridge.
He has been camping since Friday.

entries.meaning: To walk a long and difficult distance, usually in wild country. ---
examples: They trek through the mountains every spring.

She has been trekking in Nepal for a month.
entries.contrast: The k doubles: trekked, trekking — one of the few verbs where a final k is doubled.

entries.meaning: To travel or hike carrying everything you need in a backpack. ---
examples: Students backpack across Europe every summer.
They backpacked through the national park.
He has been backpacking for a month.

entries.meaning: To play golf. ---
examples: They golf every Saturday morning.

He has been golfing since he retired.

entries.meaning: To roll your body forward or backward in a complete circle. ---
examples: Divers somersault twice before entering the water.

She was somersaulting the length of the mat.
entries.contrast: Spelled -sault, not -salt, and written as one word.

entries.meaning: To make muscles firmer and stronger through exercise. ---
examples: These exercises tone the shoulders and back.

entries.meaning: To drink enough water so the body has the fluid it needs. ---
examples: Runners need to hydrate well before a long race.
She hydrated between every set.
The players have been hydrating all afternoon in this heat.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (hydrate the body), intransitive (hydrate before the race)

entries.meaning: Exert has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Do not exert yourself in this heat.

They were exerting themselves far too much in the first half.
The moon exerts a pull on the oceans.
Her father exerted enormous influence over the company.
Pressure is being exerted on the mayor to resign.

senses.head: To make a physical effort, usually with a reflexive pronoun
examples: Do not exert yourself in this heat.
He exerted himself too early in the race.
They were exerting themselves far too much in the first half.

senses.head: To apply force, pressure, or influence on something
examples: The moon exerts a pull on the oceans.
Her father exerted enormous influence over the company.
Pressure is being exerted on the mayor to resign.

entries.русский: напрягаться, прилагать усилия; оказывать (давление, влияние); прилагать (силу)
entries.contrast: Normally takes a reflexive object: exert yourself, exert himself, not just exert.

entries.meaning: To tighten painfully, said of a muscle during hard exercise. ---
examples: Legs often cramp in the last mile.
His calf cramped at the ninety-minute mark.
She has been cramping badly since halftime.

entries.meaning: To watch a sporting event instead of taking part in it. ---
examples: If your knee still hurts, just spectate today.
We spectated from the top of the hill.
Thousands were spectating along the route.

entries.meaning: In chess, to trap the opponent's king so the game is won. ---
examples: You can checkmate him in three moves from here.
She checkmated him on move twenty-nine.
He has been checkmated twice in a row.

entries.meaning: In chess, to leave the opponent with no legal move, which ends the game in a draw. ---
examples: One careless move can stalemate the game.
He stalemated his opponent and saved half a point.
The match was stalemated after forty moves.
entries.русский: приводить к пату, зайти в тупик
entries.contrast: A stalemate is a draw, not a win — unlike checkmate.

entries.meaning: To pretend to have a strong hand or position in order to fool an opponent. ---
examples: Good players bluff only when the story makes sense.

entries.transitivity: both — transitive (bluff an opponent), intransitive (he was bluffing)

entries.meaning: To risk money on the result of a game or race. ---
examples: Fans wager millions on the final every year.

More has been wagered on this game than on any other.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (wager fifty dollars), intransitive (wager on the underdog)
entries.contrast: You wager money on a team or a result.

entries.meaning: Trump has 2 distinct senses.
examples: If you have no hearts, you can trump the trick.
She trumped my ace and took the hand.
My king was trumped on the very last round.
Safety concerns trump cost every time.
Her experience trumped his connections.
In this office, speed has always trumped polish.

senses.head: In card games, to beat a card by playing one of the trump suit
examples: If you have no hearts, you can trump the trick.
She trumped my ace and took the hand.
My king was trumped on the very last round.

senses.head: To be more important than something else and so outweigh it
examples: Safety concerns trump cost every time.
Her experience trumped his connections.
In this office, speed has always trumped polish.

entries.русский: бить козырем, козырять; перевешивать, перевесить; оказываться важнее

entries.meaning: In a video game, to come back into play after your character is killed. ---
examples: You respawn at the last checkpoint.
He respawned right behind the enemy team.
The boss has respawned again.

entries.meaning: Floor has 3 distinct senses.
examples: One good right hand can floor him.
She floored her opponent in the second round.
He has been floored only once in his whole career.
The news absolutely floored me.
I was floored when they offered me the job.
Her answer is going to floor you.
He floored it and shot through the intersection.
Don't floor the gas on wet pavement.
She was flooring it the whole way home.

senses.head: To knock someone down to the ground with a punch or a hit
examples: One good right hand can floor him.
She floored her opponent in the second round.
He has been floored only once in his whole career.

senses.head: To shock or amaze someone completely
examples: The news absolutely floored me.
I was floored when they offered me the job.
Her answer is going to floor you.

senses.head: To press a car's gas pedal all the way down
body: (жать на газ до упора, вдавить педаль в пол)
examples: He floored it and shot through the intersection.
Don't floor the gas on wet pavement.
She was flooring it the whole way home.

entries.русский: сбивать с ног, отправлять в нокдаун; ошеломлять, ошеломить; поражать, сразить; жать на газ до упора, вдавить педаль в пол

entries.meaning: To fake one way and go the other in order to get past a defender.
examples: Quick running backs juke defenders in the open field.
He juked the safety and walked into the end zone.
She was juking past defenders all game.
entries.contrast: Informal but very common in American sports talk. The silent e drops: juked, juking.
